newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices rise again at Christchurch sale.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices rise again at Christchurch sale.

text.p: Wool prices firmed again at a wool sale in Christchurch on Thursday after they gained sharply at last week's sales, Wools of New Zealand said.
The market indicator gained seven cents to 448 cents with the fine segment down 16 to 806, strong up eight to 399 and the lamb segment up eight to 410.
Main buying interest came from Nepal, Turkey, Western Europe and China with support from Australia, the United States, India and local mills.
Some 17 percent of the 1,486 tonnes on offer was passed in. The offering was dominated by crossbred fleece which made up 74 percent.

Crossbred 32 and 33 micron prices were unchanged, with 35 micron and stronger 3-4 percent dearer. Merino was 2.5 percent cheaper, halfbred fleece one percent cheaper, cotts and second shear 3-4 percent dearer, first lambs up to 2.5 percent dearer, bulky skirtings five percent dearer and second shear bellies and pieces generally unchanged.
The next sales will be at Napier and Christchurch on February 5. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
